data.body: S2 plan-review v4: blocking=1, and it was the BEST finding yet — a genuine architectural hole S1 created. S1 deliberately leaves openai/google as LAZY MODEL STRINGS (not objects) so their optional SDKs need not be importable. But capabilities_for() reads model.profile, and getattr(str, profile, None) is None -> conservative fallback -> native_structured_output=False -> openai/google SILENTLY lose NativeOutput, which test_structured.py:177 asserts against. RESOLVED with a verified asymmetry: pydantic_ai.profiles.* are PURE capability records that import WITHOUT the vendor SDK (confirmed: openai/google/groq SDKs all ABSENT from the venv, yet openai_model_profile(gpt-4o).supports_json_schema_output returns True), whereas pydantic_ai.providers.openai raises ImportError. So capabilities_for() now accepts a model OBJECT or a model STRING, resolving the latter through a single _PROFILE_RESOLVERS registry into pydantic_ai.profiles.* — rebar can read capabilities for a provider it cannot construct, exactly the asymmetry S1s lazy path needs. Added an AC pinning that a lazy openai:gpt-4o string still yields native_structured_output=True (i.e. the fallback is NOT reached for a merely-deferred provider). Also added runner.py:28 import as an explicit Scope edit target (v3s two duplicate blockers). Re-reviewing.
